entrada.titulo: A secure and trustworthy blockchain-assisted edge computing architecture for industrial internet of things

perfil_anterior.problema: Centralized data storage is a big obstacle.
perfil_anterior.avaliacao: the proposed architecture lowers the authentication time and obtains a high response rate
perfil_anterior.possibilidades: Integrar SSI para gerenciamento de identidade descentralizada nas bordas; avaliar criptografia baseada em atributos (ABE) para controle de acesso granular nos dados de borda; comparar o consenso PoAh com PBFT ou PoS quanto a latência e consumo energético; testar a arquitetura em múltiplas cidades inteligentes para validar interoperabilidade e escalabilidade; analisar conformidade com regulamentos de privacidade (ex.: GDPR) no contexto de dados industriais.

entrada.texto:
a blockchain-based management architecture is suggested in 22. The structure would use smart contracts 
and blockchain technology to offer trustworthy services independent of any third party. Additionally 23, uses 
blockchain technology to record the hash values of sensitive data and provide tracking services, ensuring 
accuracy and accountability.
Edge computing can also benefit from blockchain smart contracts, increasing its security. To improve 
the reliability of collaborative edge computing (CEC), the authors of 24 introduce BlockEdge, an application 
framework driven by blockchain technology. Based on the on-chain validation findings and deposit balances, 
BlockEdge builds a trust rating system. To address the need for a trust assessment method and to maintain 
privacy in the context of trust management and data security, a new blockchain called TrustChain is suggested25. 
A blockchain-based trust process for transferring task analyzing in mobile edge computing (MEC) is offered 
in26. This mechanism aims to avoid incidents of self-centered edge servers and counterfeit service records 
by deploying a blockchain to store and handle trust data. Additionally, it develops a consensus protocol that 
combines PoW and PoS.
The methods for allocating CPUs and evaluating trust on edge servers are not just individual implementations, 
but collaborative efforts that draw from two different schools of thought-RL and DRL. Both these approaches are 
harnessed to optimize the number of CPUs on edge servers, thereby reducing their computational consumption 
and evaluating their service reliability using Bayesian reasoning. By employing convolutional neural networks 
(CNNs) to reduce the current state space and incorporating an altered Boltzmann distribution to achieve the 
appropriate number of CPUs, the latter method promises to further enhance computational speed. The steps for 
controlling access among devices and gateway nodes, gateway nodes and servers at the edge, and cloud servers 
are all part of a consortium blockchain-enabled access control initiative in edge computing-based generic IoT 
environments, as suggested in 27. This collaborative effort is set to redefine access control in edge computing. 
To fortify data against attacks such as identity-revealing, session hijacking, relay, and man-in-the-middle, a 
decentralized security system has been developed in28 using blockchain technology and edge computing. This is 
a testament to the power of collaboration in the face of common threats.
Zhang et al.29 presented the application of industrial IoT for effective certificate-less signing in cloud-assisted 
systems. For data reliability and third-party security, lightweight certificate-less verification is ideal. Reliable 
certificateless signatures (RCLS) prevent signature forgeries. A secure sharing mechanism was proposed by Zheng 
and Cai30 to ensure the privacy of IIoT data, which is significant in the context of increasing concerns about data 
privacy and security in IIoT systems. The main features of this system are data sharing upon request and profit-
based differentiated privacy. From confidentiality of information to bandwidth utilization, this framework excels 
at IoT security considerations. A credit-based consensus method is the basis for Secure IIoT. An IoT device PoW 
system based on credits was discussed by Huang et al.31. The IoT device sensitive information is safeguarded by 
blockchain ledger.
Zhu et al.32 discussed an IIoT-directed network for secure identification. The third-party and the authorized 
user have a secure connection. The encryption accumulator is an element of the direct graph that facilitates 
this process. An adaptable signature system is employed to ensure the safety of data trade. Using blockchain 
technology and federated learning, Lu et al. 33 suggested a method for exchanging data in IIoT that preserves 
users’ privacy. This method involves a combination of blockchain technology and federated learning to ensure 
data privacy and security in IoT systems. In maintained federated learning, data exchange is implemented so 
that different people can engage with the computer. To train their datasets, privacy-preserving and federated 
approaches both purchase blockchain technology. A deep belief network–based supervisory control and data 
collecting system was introduced by Huda et al. 34. The writer devised ensemble techniques for deep belief 
learning and categorization. System control is accomplished using the industrial control system. Both the traffic 
and payload features are handled.
The IIoT uses a private data protector to prevent confidential data leakage. To keep an eye on data and 
adjust the distributed defense assault, Wu et al.35 suggested a hierarchical analytical procedure and approach for 
ordering preferences based on their similarity to an ideal answer. The use of the Ethereum blockchain and deep 
reinforcement learning in tandem36 for gathering and exchanging data from industrial IoT devices is another 
key aspect. However, it’s the consideration of sensor distance and power sources that truly aids in obtaining 
high-quality data, a crucial piece of information that our audience will find enlightening. This is accomplished 
using intelligent mobile terminals, efficiently exchanging data and gathering trustworthy information. Most of 
the data may be obtained by employing DRL. The dataset is allocated to ensure the input contributors’ security 
using federated deep learning. The lightweight technique’s multi-contributors are guaranteed vital privacy 
preservation.
Gai et al. 37 built IIoT based on a blockchain that uses asymmetrical privacy. This piece aims to bridge the 
gap between blockchain IoT and BIoE. The IoT may create a privacy-indicating energy cost indicator using its 
controls. Data is collected in a way that doesn’t impact power consumption. Zhou et al.38 suggested a public key 
encrypted text for industrial IoT devices to use in lightweight, safe searching. Edge devices, which are computing 
devices that operate at the edge of the network, are used to enable cryptographic activities in communication 
between edge devices. The goal is to safeguard the edge device as it makes quick computations.
The rising significance of safe and effective data processing systems to handle the massive amounts of data 
produced by industrial applications is highlighted in the above literature. Because edge computing can process 
data closer to the source, reducing latency and bandwidth usage has become an essential component. Traditional 
edge and cloud-based approaches frequently need more security and confidence than blockchain’s decentralized, 
immutable ledger provides. Related work has investigated several frameworks that combine edge computing and 
blockchain to manage identities, encrypt data, and preserve integrity among dispersed devices in IIoT networks. 
However, the adoption of many existing models in IIoT systems with limited resources could be improved by 
scalability, energy consumption, and interoperability issues. Limitations still exist despite these developments,

resposta.resumo: O trecho revisa diversas propostas que combinam blockchain e computação de borda para IIoT, destacando arquiteturas de gestão baseadas em contratos inteligentes, sistemas de confiança como BlockEdge e TrustChain, e mecanismos de controle de acesso em ambientes genéricos de IoT. Aponta que, apesar dos avanços, ainda há limitações de escalabilidade, consumo energético e interoperabilidade que precisam ser superadas para adoção em larga escala.

possibilidades: Avaliar a integração de SSI (Self‑Sovereign Identity) para gerenciamento descentralizado de identidade nas bordas.
Implementar controle de acesso baseado em Attribute‑Based Encryption (ABE) para granularidade maior.
Comparar o consenso híbrido PoW/PoS usado em TrustChain com PBFT ou PoS em termos de latência e consumo energético.
Testar a arquitetura em múltiplas cidades inteligentes para validar interoperabilidade e escalabilidade.
Investigar conformidade com regulamentos de privacidade (ex.: GDPR) no contexto de dados industriais.
